issues.title: Dimensionally invalid diffusion orientation in the Feynman–Kac formula
issues.failure_explanation: The source declares u to map R^d to R^p, so its Jacobian has size p by d, and declares sigma to have size d by q. Thus the old product (nabla_x u) sigma^top attempts to multiply a p by d matrix by a q by d matrix and is not conformable for general d and q. Multiplication by sigma instead gives the required p by q value of Z and matches the generator's z-domain. The old remark rmk_dsEZs already uses this corrected orientation.
issues.overall_effect: The stated Feynman–Kac representation and associated PDE are malformed for the paper's general dimensions, and the analytical chain using that representation is valid only under the uniquely forced corrected reading.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace ∇_x u σ^T by ∇_x u σ in eq_Ytut and in the corresponding argument of f in the PDE, and interpret all references to the Feynman–Kac formula using this corrected p-by-q quantity.
issues.why_classification: The declared p-by-d Jacobian and d-by-q diffusion matrix uniquely force multiplication by σ, and rmk_dsEZs already uses that orientation. The transpose makes the expression ill-typed rather than expressing a coherent alternative guarantee; no inference, hypothesis, rate, or dependent result needs alteration.

issues.title: Variable-direction differentiation destroys branch-permutation invariance

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In \eqref{eq_recur_F}, the partial derivatives $\partial_{\theta}$ also act on $F_s^{\Upsilon_i}$.

issues.failure_explanation: For two branch directions V and W, the old instruction gives a commutator difference (V·partial)(W·partial)F-(W·partial)(V·partial)F equal to ((V·partial)W-(W·partial)V)·partial F, which is generally nonzero. Yet def_equival_T identifies trees differing only by the order of those branches, and prop_Labs_equ claims their elementary differentials coincide. Freezing V and W while differentiating only the base function turns the expression into the symmetric multilinear derivative required by the later Taylor expansion.
issues.overall_effect: The old elementary differential is not invariant on the stated tree equivalence classes, so the ULN-tree differential and the error expansion based on regrouping equivalent trees are not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Amend def_elediff so that, during the θ-differentiations, the branch values F_s^{Υ_1},…,F_s^{Υ_l} are held fixed and the expression is the symmetric l-linear θ-derivative of F_t(s,Θ_s) applied to those branch values. The outer s-derivatives should still act on all s-dependence. Add the routine mixed-partial-symmetry justification for prop_Labs_equ and use this reading throughout the Taylor expansion.
issues.why_classification: The explicit instruction that θ-derivatives also act on the direction fields creates genuine commutator terms, so this is not a transcriptional typo. Nevertheless, the required repair is local and is already forced by the ordinary multivariate Taylor expansion used later. Symmetry and the regrouping by tree equivalence then follow routinely, with no change to the method, order conditions, rates, or listed dependent conclusions.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: the partial derivatives $\partial_{\theta}$ do not act on $F_s^{\Upsilon_1}, F_s^{\Upsilon_2}, \cdots, F_s^{\Upsilon_l}$

issues.title: Unestablished endpoint limits for elementary differentials

failure_location.quote: By Taylor's expansion of $s \mapsto F_{t, s}^{[\;]_0}$ at $s = t$

issues.failure_explanation: The elementary differentials are introduced through limits as s approaches t, but the old source provides no result proving that these limits exist or that the recursively defined functions have the uniform endpoint differentiability needed by the Taylor expansions in the proof. This is nontrivial because the second component of F_t contains the singular factor (s-t)^{-1}. Consequently, thm_taylor invokes unestablished objects and endpoint expansions. The latest source addresses this same root with prop_existence_F and revised regularity assumptions.
issues.overall_effect: The old error expansion, and hence the formal consistency and convergence chain derived from it, lacks a proved endpoint-regularity foundation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen assu_regu only to a concretely sufficient finite smoothness level—for example u in C_b^{r+1,2r+4} and f in C_b^{r+1,2r+3,2r+3,2r+3}, together with the needed moment condition on X_0—and insert an endpoint-regularity lemma. Using Gaussian integration by parts or the Stein identity, Dynkin differentiation, and induction on trees, prove that every F_{t,s}^{Υ} required for |Υ|≤r+1 exists, extends to s=t from the right, and has the uniform endpoint derivatives and remainder bounds used in eq_Fts and eq_taylor_Ftninj. Then invoke that lemma in thm_taylor and retain the existing consistency and convergence deductions.
issues.why_classification: Cancellation of the apparent (s−t)^{-1} singularity and propagation of endpoint regularity through the recursive elementary differentials require a contained but nontrivial new lemma and induction, not a routine local edit. This work does not require new global proof architecture, and only finite technical regularity is added; the error expansion, order, convergence rate, method, and intended smooth regime remain recognizably unchanged. Thus a complete moderate repair is established.

issues.title: Stabilizer overcount in the tree error expansion
issues.failure_explanation: For Upsilon=[[ ]_0[ ]_0]_0, the ordered tuple containing two identical branches occurs once and retains the quadratic Taylor factor 1/2!. The old rewrite nevertheless multiplies B_i^m by N_P=2, although those two stabilizing permutations yield the same tuple. With alpha=1, S=2, and gamma=2, the theorem therefore assigns coefficient 1 instead of 1/2. The latest proof omits this stabilizer multiplier and obtains B_i^m=A_i^m/gamma.
issues.overall_effect: The exact coefficients in thm_taylor are wrong for trees with repeated identical branches. The sufficient order conditions based on setting A_0^m to zero are unchanged, because the erroneous factor is nonzero and does not affect vanishing.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: When converting the ordered branch-tuple sum into a sum over LN-trees, count each tuple once and do not multiply B_i^m(Υ) by the stabilizer N_P(Υ). Accordingly use A_i^m(Υ)/γ(Υ) as the LN-tree coefficient and α(Υ)A_i^m(Υ)/γ(Υ) as the ULN-tree coefficient, rather than coefficients containing S(Υ). Update the corresponding formulas in thm_taylor and its proof; the symmetry statistic may be retained as unused notation or removed.
issues.why_classification: The stabilizer factor comes from an invalid combinatorial regrouping, so the issue is substantive rather than typographical. Its correction is nevertheless a short, local orbit-counting adjustment requiring no new lemma or proof architecture. The same exact-expansion theorem survives with corrected coefficients, while the vanishing order conditions and all associated rates remain unchanged.

issues.title: Undefined maximum of vector-valued local errors
issues.failure_explanation: The local error R^n is the difference of two values of Theta and therefore lies in R^p times R^{p by q}. Such vectors have no maximum under the paper's definitions. The preceding expansion supplies a uniform bound on their magnitude, and the old definition of big-O is explicitly phrased through absolute value. Thus the argument supports max_n |R^n|, not the literal statement max_n R^n.
issues.overall_effect: The consistency theorem's displayed conclusion is not a well-defined scalar estimate, and the later convergence argument needs the magnitude bound that the proof actually supplies.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the conclusion by max_{0≤n≤N−1}|R^n|=O((Δt)^{r+1}), where |·| is the norm on R^p×R^{p×q}, and use that scalar magnitude estimate in subsequent references.
issues.why_classification: R^n is explicitly vector-valued, while the preceding expansion and the paper's definition of big-O already provide a uniform bound on |R^n|. The omitted norm bars are uniquely forced by the old source, and restoring them requires no change to the proof or any downstream rate.

issues.title: Missing root exclusion in the definition of T_{r-}
issues.failure_explanation: The old definition places a tree in T_{r-} when [ ]_0 is not one of its branches. The tree [ ]_0 has order one and, by def_branch_ntree, has no branches; it therefore satisfies the literal definition and belongs to T_{1-}. The proof of prop_Cr_table nevertheless invokes T_{1-}=empty. That premise is false under the active definitions, although the proposition's conclusion is easily recoverable because C(r) already treats A_i^m([ ]_0)=0 in its separate first line.
issues.overall_effect: The listed sets and their cardinalities are inconsistent with the literal definition, and the r=1 proof of prop_Cr_table uses a false premise. The substantive order conditions are unchanged because the root-tree condition was already imposed separately.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine T_{r−} as {Υ in T_r : Υ≠[ ]_0 and [ ]_0 is not a branch of Υ}. With this one exclusion, the displayed enumerations, cardinalities, and the proof of prop_Cr_table are consistent; the separately imposed condition A_i^m([ ]_0)=0 remains unchanged.
issues.why_classification: Under the literal, otherwise coherent branch definition, the root tree vacuously satisfies the stated condition, so identifying and resolving the exceptional root case requires a small mathematical check rather than merely reading through malformed notation. The repair is a single local qualification already supported by the separate root condition and the stated enumeration, and it causes no change to the substantive order conditions or proposition conclusion.
